about.title: Milpitas Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Milpitas sits where I-880, I-680 and Route 237 come together, and in 2025 the city recorded 243 injury collisions with 318 people hurt. Four of those crashes took a life. Behind each number is a household in Santa Clara County trying to work out what comes next, often while handling a funeral and an insurer that keeps calling. A wrongful death claim is the civil path for those left behind. It stands apart from any criminal charges, and it exists to account for what the family actually lost: burial and funeral expenses, the income and support the person would have provided, and the love, companionship and guidance no paycheck can measure. California generally gives you two years from the date of death to file, but that window narrows sharply when a city, county or state agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Milpitas families with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless something is recovered. The first conversation costs nothing.

whyChoose.title: What a Milpitas Family Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Only certain relatives can bring the claim
items.desc: California gives the first right to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children; certain dependents and heirs may qualify when those relatives are absent. An attorney can sort out who belongs on the case before anything is filed.

items.title: The clock runs from the date of death
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years, but if a government entity such as Caltrans or the City of Milpitas may share fault, a formal claim is due much sooner. Waiting to ask can close a door that cannot be reopened.

items.title: The losses counted are broader than a funeral bill
items.desc: A claim may seek funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided over time, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Each category needs its own documentation.

items.question: My spouse was killed in a crash on I-880 near Milpitas. Does it matter that the freeway is state-maintained?
items.answer: It can. If the condition of the roadway or its signage played any part, a claim against a public agency may be involved, and that path carries a much shorter deadline than the standard two years. An attorney will usually want to look at that question early, alongside the driver's insurance.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do I have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death action is a separate civil matter with its own timeline and a lower standard of proof. Some families choose to move forward while the criminal case is pending so evidence is preserved and deadlines are protected.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge a fee for connecting us?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, and we do not take a percentage of anything. The independent attorney we connect you with works on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery, and you decide whether to hire them after the first conversation.
